title: Device specification block
description: Hardware specs that determine local-inference performance. This block lives inside a hardware record (data/hardware/<id>.json) as the 'device' key — that is the single source of truth. A setup may carry the same block under data/setups/<id>.json 'device' only as a measurement-specific override (e.g. an overclocked card); it never re-describes the whole class. Rule of the dataset: bandwidth sets the decode roofline, memory capacity sets what fits, and any figure a vendor does not publish stays null with a note — never a guess.

identity.description: Who made it and what it is called. Required so a spec block is never anonymous.

name.description: Human-readable device or class name, e.g. 'NVIDIA DGX Spark'

chip.description: Processor architecture as the vendor names it, e.g. 'GB10 Grace Blackwell', 'Apple M4 Pro', 'AD102 (Ada Lovelace)'

os.description: Operating system the specs describe, e.g. 'DGX OS (Ubuntu)'. null when the class spans hosts (discrete-GPU records).

sku.description: Exact product code when the record is one SKU, e.g. NVIDIA '940-54242-0000'

total_gb.description: Total RAM/VRAM in GB. On class records this is the class ceiling, matching the hardware record's memory_gb.

bandwidth_gbs.description: Memory bandwidth in GB/s — the strongest hardware predictor of low-concurrency decode speed. null on class records whose variants each carry their own bandwidth.

interface_bits.description: Memory bus width, e.g. 256 for GB10, 384 for RTX 3090/4090

channels.description: Memory channel count. Only include when the vendor publishes it — GB10's 256-bit interface does not imply a channel count.

unified.description: true when CPU and GPU share one memory pool (Apple Silicon, GB10). false for discrete VRAM.

usable_gb.description: Practically usable capacity after OS/runtime reserves, matching the hardware record's memory_usable_gb

compute.description: Vendor-published compute peaks. Every value here is a theoretical peak for the named precision; null means the vendor does not publish it — third-party estimates do not belong in the dataset. Tensor figures are NOT interchangeable across precisions: FP8 sparse ≠ FP16 dense.

cpu_cores.description: CPU description, e.g. '20-core Arm: 10x Cortex-X925 + 10x Cortex-A725'

fp32_tflops.description: Shader/CUDA FP32 peak, e.g. RTX 3090 35.6, RTX 4090 83 (NVIDIA's published figure)

fp16_sparse_tflops.description: Structured-sparsity marketing figure; state the accumulation mode in the note when the vendor does

fp8_dense_tflops.description: null when the architecture has no native FP8 tensor path (Ampere)

fp4_sparse_pflops.description: Blackwell-era FP4 peak with sparsity, in PFLOPs, e.g. GB10 = 1.0

tensor_ai_tops.description: Vendor 'AI TOPS' marketing figure when no clean TFLOPS is published, e.g. RTX 4090 = 1321 (FP8, sparse)

neural_engine_tops.description: Apple Neural Engine, TOPS. Apple publishes 38 for the M4 family. Note honestly that current MLX and llama.cpp paths mostly drive the GPU, not the ANE.

note.description: Required context for every non-null figure here; also where 'unpublished' is explained

storage.description: Affects model load time and streamed-expert performance. Omit entirely on records where storage is host-dependent (discrete-GPU classes).

read_gbs.description: Sequential read, GB/s. null when the vendor does not publish it.

thermal.description: Power and cooling context — sustained-load behavior is why two boxes with equal bandwidth can drift apart under load.

tdp_watts.description: Chip or board TDP/TGP as the vendor states it; say which in the note

psu_watts.description: System power supply or max continuous system power

variants.description: For class records only: the exact SKUs the class covers, each with its own verified numbers. Every variant bandwidth must fall inside the hardware record's bandwidth_range_gbs. Unique ids.

memory_configs.description: RAM configurations this SKU ships in, e.g. '24-64 GB'

sources.description: Provenance law applies to specs too: every published figure traces to the vendor page or datasheet cited here.
